All ports are on the FRONT in TWO BANKS of sixteen stacked columns, with two 25G SFP28 in-band management cages, an RJ-45 management jack, a USB 3.0 Type-A storage port, an RJ-45 console, a ToD jack, 1PPS and 10 MHz timing jacks, six system lamps and a reset button; two 3000 W supplies and FOUR fan trays are on the rear. Its twin edgecore/ais800-64o is the same chassis with an OSFP800 wall. This is NOT a taller AIS800-32D: the 32-port models are a 438.4 x 589 x 44 shell with seven 1RU trays and 2400 W Saf-D-Grid supplies, and this is a 440 x 649.2 x 87 shell with four 2RU trays and 3000 W C20 supplies. The quick start guide's System LEDs/Buttons page lists the six chassis lamps and the RJ-45's pair and stops; the datasheet names port, management-port and system LEDs and no module lamp. THE SUPPLIES CARRY NONE: the only round features on the AC supply's face are the two Phillips screw heads at its corners, which is the AIS800-32D's finding for the same vendor's supplies. The four rate colours are declared because they are named; whether the window also blinks for activity, and what it shows for link without traffic, is not published. A port-LED table, or one photograph of a lit port at a known speed, settles it.","what":"port-lamp-speed-colours"},{"reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["rear"],"wanted":"What the DC supply's six-bore input connector actually is. Signal -\", with 1 on both left bores, 2 on both right, 3 on the upper centre and 4 on the lower - and the datasheet gives the rating and the wire gauge. NEITHER NAMES THE CONNECTOR. That is the difference from this line's AC inlets, which both documents name outright (this model's \"IEC 60320 C20\", the AIS800-32D's \"Anderson Saf D Grid\"), and it matters because a named part gets the manufacturer's own drawing and an unnamed one gets a figure measured at 7.18 px/mm. edgecore/ais800-64-psu-dc@1 is drawn to that figure and says so. The datasheet's page 2 carries a rear photograph of each build side by side under the headings \"Airflow: Front-to-back\" and \"Airflow: Back-to-front\": red tray bars and red PSU latches on the first, blue on the second. The ordering table pairs PSU-AC-3000W-F and FAN-2U-1x1SN-F with front-to-back and the -B parts with back-to-front and names no colour. See roc-ops/Portrayal#277. THE RULE COVERS THE AC LATCH AND THE TRAY BARS AND NOTHING ELSE. Sampled on those two photographs the AC latch reads #dd3d12 front-to-back and #6186db back-to-front, and the tray bars #fe3c42 and #469dfb. THE DC SUPPLY'S LATCH IS GREEN AND STAYS GREEN: the only images of that face are the guide's Connect Power figure and its Chinese copy, both of which draw it #9cdb7d on a page with no red pixel on it, and no photograph of a DC build exists in the staged corpus. The dc-b2f configuration therefore recolours the tray bars and leaves the supply alone. An earlier model painted that latch red and blue by analogy with the AC unit, which was the airflow rule reaching one part further than its evidence. THE TWO BUILDS ARE DERATED DIFFERENTLY: front-to-back 0-40 C and back-to-front 0-35 C, \"subject to used optics\", both at 1800 m."},"gate-1":{"confidence":"measured","note":"PASSES. The front elevation reads 2224 x 442 px at 600 dpi; 2224/440 is 5.0545 px/mm and 442/87 is 5.0805 - 0.5% apart. The rear reads 2228 x 442: 5.0636 and 5.0805, 0.3% apart. Each face is measured on its own x scale, and the two are 0.2% apart from each other, so neither carries the other's numbers. THE DRAWINGS ARE UPSCALES AND THAT WAS CHECKED, as the 32-port models' were. The datasheet's page-2 photographs are embedded at 3.67 px/mm and were scanned at their own scale as an independent instrument; every rear edge below agrees between the two within 0.5 mm, which is what stops a 600 dpi render of a 1.8 px/mm raster from being believed on its own."},"power":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"3000 W PER SUPPLY, stated three times: the datasheet's feature list (\"Hot-swappable, load-sharing, redundant 3000 W AC/DC PSUs\"), its power section (\"PSUs: 2 redundant, load-sharing, hot-swappable 3000 W AC/DC\") and the housing's own \"3000W\" label in the rear photograph. INPUT. AC: \"200-240 VAC at 50-60Hz (16 A/3000 W max.)\" with the inlet named outright - \"AC PSU Inlet: IEC 60320 C20\" - and a C19-C20 cord in the -UN builds. DC: \"-48 V ~ -60 V (80 A/3000 W max.)\". There is no low-line AC rating anywhere, and the guide adds that a single supply powering a fully loaded system must be on 200-240 VAC. DRAW IS STATED ONCE AND IT IS A CEILING, NOT A TYPICAL: \"Less than 2775 W (100% traffic at 40 C ambient temperature with 100% fan speed and 64 x 18 W optics)\". No typical figure is published, so none is recorded - unlike the AIS800-32D, which publishes both. THE PER-PORT BUDGET IS 30 W, qualified by the datasheet itself: every one of the 64 ports, on both the OSFP and the QSFP-DD800 version, can take up to 30 W, but how many are actually populated at that figure is bounded by the total power distribution and by thermal limits."},"sources":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"A QUICK START GUIDE AND A DATASHEET, AND FOR ONCE THEY AGREE ABOUT THE CHASSIS. Both are staged: ais800-64d-qsg (8 pages, bilingual, 69 figures) and ais800-64d-datasheet (5 pages, 4 figures). The guide carries the Overview elevations, a System LEDs/Buttons enlargement, the FRU replacement figures and a Connect Power page that draws the DC supply's face; the datasheet carries photographs of BOTH airflow builds, the ordering tables and the power ratings. The guide's specification table reads \"440 x 649.2 x 87 mm (17.32 x 25.56 x 3.43 in.)\" and the datasheet \"44 x 64.92 x 8.7 cm (17.32 x 25.56 x 3.43 in.)\" - the same numbers in different units, which the AIS800-32D's two documents notably did not manage. THE WEIGHT IS THE ONE DISAGREEMENT: the guide says 21.2 kg \"with 2 PSUs and 4 fans installed\" and the datasheet 21.5 kg \"with 2 PSUs and 4 fan modules installed\". Both are recorded; 21.2 is used because the guide is the document that also carries the measured elevations. FIVE PHOTOGRAPHS ARE STAGED and unlike the 32-port models' they are worth something: at 960 x 700 over a 440 mm face they are 2.18 px/mm, but the DATASHEET's own page-2 photographs render at 8.99 px/mm and were measured beside the drawing throughout."},"stack-orientation":{"confidence":"estimated","note":"The library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md, S1-S4): a row pair is the upper cage upright (rotate 0) over the lower turned 180, so both cage lips face the band between the two cages and both bails face outward. Decided by the port lamps, which point up over down: the 1 SFP pair (mgmt-inband-1/mgmt-inband-2). Decided by the rule, not an observation, so a photograph of the stack overturns it: the 32 QSFP-DD pairs (port-1/port-2 to port-63/port-64)."},"the-ac-inlet-is-named-c20-and-the-photograph-agrees-about-everything-but-the-blades":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"THE DOCUMENTS NAME IT THREE TIMES: the datasheet's power section reads \"AC PSU Inlet: IEC 60320 C20\", its ordering table ships an \"IEC 60320 C19-C20 power cord\" with the -UN builds, and the guide's package contents list \"AC Power cord, type IEC C19\". That is as explicit as this vendor gets, and it is why std/c20-inlet@1 is the part. THE PHOTOGRAPH'S PIN GEOMETRY AGREES. Measured on the datasheet's rear photograph at 8.99 px/mm, the three blades sit at (74.08, 15.52), (65.68, 22.03) and (73.64, 28.98): a pair 13.46 mm apart with the third blade 8.4 mm off their line, which is the C19/C20 triangle, and each blade is about 1 x 3 mm, which is a C19/C20 blade. The part is turned so that pair stands vertical at the right and the odd blade sits at the left, which is `rotate: 270` and is what the render draws. WHAT DOES NOT AGREE IS THE BLADES' OWN ORIENTATION. On the photograph each blade is narrow and TALL - its long axis parallel to the line joining the pair. std/c20-inlet@1 draws its blades across that line, so once the part is turned they come out short and wide. THAT DETAIL IS UNSOURCED IN THE PART: its contract says the recess and pins are \"proportional from the same drawing, NOT dimensioned\", and the SCHURTER drawing it cites dimensions the panel cutout only. So this is the shared part's unsourced detail and not a wrong part on this device, and it is not silently corrected here on the strength of one photograph: eleven modules across five vendors seat std/c20-inlet@1 and they would all move. See roc-ops/Portrayal#398."},"the-grounding-point":{"confidence":"measured","note":"A BRIGHT PLATE WITH TWO HOLES at the far left of the rear, x 1.34-14.47 by y 30.27-66.21 on the photograph, the holes at (7.2, 39.8) and (7.4, 56.0) about 4.2 across. The guide says what they are: the rear-panel grounding point, where a grounding wire is fixed with two M6 screws and washers through a grounding lug (Panduit LCDXN2-14AF-E or an equivalent), and the QSG's Overview callout 5 reads \"2 x grounding screws\". An earth symbol is silkscreened above the plate at (7.4, 26.1) and the supply legend \"(up) PSU1 / (down) PSU2\" above that."},"the-management-cluster":{"confidence":"measured","note":"EVERY ITEM MEASURED ON THE ENLARGEMENT AT 15 px/mm, which is the best-resolved figure either AIS800 model has. TWO 25G SFP28 CAGES IN ONE BEZEL at x 398.45-413.20, apertures y 16.08-26.04 and 31.38-41.34 - 14.75 x 9.96 against std/sfp@1's 14.5 x 10.0, on a 15.30 row pitch. The bezel's middle band carries the pair's two lamps. AN RJ-45 MANAGEMENT JACK at 416.46-432.27 - 15.81 wide against std/rj45@2's 15.8, which is as close as a drawing gets - with its own pair of lamps at the top corners, which is what common/rj45-eth@1 draws. A USB 3.0 TYPE-A BENEATH IT, opening 418.09-430.58 by 35.08-39.56: 12.49 x 4.48 against std/usb-a@1's 12.0 x 4.5. THE TONGUE IS BLUE in both the enlargement and the datasheet photograph, so the `default` skin is right and `usb2` would be a false claim. The documents call it \"USB3.0 storage port\" and draw a Type-A; the AIS800-32D's is a Type-C. Two models of one series, two different connectors, both read off their own drawings. A CONSOLE AND A ToD JACK STACKED at 416.25-432.53, the pair spanning y 54.14-79.41, which is two std/rj45@2 at 13.2 with nothing to spare. TWO SMA TIMING JACKS at 406.78-413.30, y 54.34-59.76 and 62.90-68.18 - 6.5 across against std/sma@1's 6.35 - legended 1PPS above and 10MHz below. SIX SYSTEM LAMPS AND A RESET BUTTON. The lamps are rounded rectangles about 1.3 x 1.0 in a recessed strip, each directly below its legend, on a 6.1 mm pitch from 400.3 to 430.8; the guide names every one. common/led-rect-sm@1 at 2.8 x 1.6 and common/reset-button@1 at 4.0 are both larger than the drawing, and are seated at the measured CENTRES rather than the measured sizes, as the AIS800-32D's are and for the same reason: the indicator vocabulary is what a reader compares across devices."},"the-optical-wall":{"confidence":"measured","note":"SIXTY-FOUR PORTS IN TWO BANKS OF SIXTEEN STACKED COLUMNS, and the bank structure is the whole difference from the 32-port model. Each column is one bezel holding an upper aperture, a bright honeycomb band and a lower aperture; the upper bank's columns are legended `N (up) (down) N+1` ABOVE them and the lower bank's BELOW, so ports 1-32 are the upper bank and 33-64 the lower. The guide's enlargement prints `25 (up) (down) 26` over the upper bank's thirteenth column and `57 (up) (down) 58` under the lower bank's, which is the arithmetic confirmed at both ends. THE ASSEMBLY IS BUILT AROUND THE APERTURE'S CENTRE, NOT ITS TOP EDGE, and the first model of this device was not. std/qsfp-dd@1's registry opening is 10.0 tall where this panel draws 8.51; hanging the block from the drawn aperture's top edge put all 1.49 mm of the surplus at the BOTTOM of every assembly, and at review that showed as a border under the lower bank's screens that the upper bank's did not have, and as a gasket row that could only be drawn at one end. Centring the registry aperture on the drawn one splits the surplus, 0.745 mm each way, and every part of the assembly is then placed from the block's own y: 0.55 mm of shell either side of the 19.0 aperture, a gasket row at each end, and the screen filling exactly the space between the two apertures. The two banks come out identical, which is what the hardware is. ONE ROW PITCH IS USED FOR BOTH BANKS. Fitted separately they give 17.61 (upper) and 17.41 (lower) - 0.2 mm apart, which is one pixel on a 5.05 px/mm elevation - and the hardware is plainly one cage assembly used twice. 17.51 is the mean and puts every row within 0.1 mm of where it was measured. THE PITCH IS 24.019 AND BOTH BANKS WERE FITTED SEPARATELY. Aperture edges scanned along four separate row bands give left-edge fits of 24.0209 (upper) and 24.0171 (lower) with an rms of 0.06 mm, and centre fits of 24.0194 and 24.0175 with an rms of 0.035. Four independent fits inside 0.004 mm of each other is one pitch, and 24.019 is used for both. There is no ganging: the residuals alternate by a tenth of a millimetre, which is the drawing's half-pixel and not a block structure. ROWS. Aperture spans down one column read 14.64-23.15, 32.25-40.76, 48.27-56.58 and 65.68-74.39 - row pitches of 17.61 within the upper bank and 17.41 within the lower, 33.63 between the banks. The drawn openings are 18.28 x 8.51 against std/qsfp-dd@1's registry 19.0 x 10.0, the same consistent bias the EXP100 and the AIS800-32D both record: the registry owns the aperture and the device owns the pitch. THE INTER-ROW BAND IS DRAWN ON A BACKING RECT, for the reason vent-field-needs-backing-rect exists - panel pattern decor paints only its holes, and this band is BRIGHT: a white honeycomb web between the two apertures of each column, reading 24.33-31.85 in the upper bank and 57.18-64.50 in the lower. Thirty-two bands, one per column per bank, because the band belongs to the cage assembly and stops at the dark post between columns."},"the-panel-is-honeycombed-and-that-is-a-change-from-the-32-port-shell":{"confidence":"measured","note":"THE PERFORATION IS HEXAGONAL, not the slot field the AIS800-32D carries. Autocorrelation of the dark mask across the top margin gives an x period of 3.59 mm and down the bottom margin a row period of 3.07, which is a regular honeycomb of 3.59 mm pitch. The library's `vent` motif is a hex field on an 8.86 x 5.11 tile, scaled here by pattern-pitch to put its hexes on the measured 3.59; the motif's own row spacing is denser than the hardware's and that is the motif's, not a reading. THE FIELDS: a top band y 0.60-8.60 and a bottom band 78.50-86.50 across the port wall, a left column x 0.60-5.60 between them, a right column x 433.60-439.50 outside the cluster, and two fields inside the cluster itself - above the SFP28 bezel and below the reset button - which the enlargement resolves hexagon by hexagon. THE COLOUR IS SAMPLED FROM BOTH SOURCES AND THEY DISAGREE BY THEIR LIGHTING. Panel medians between features read #5d5e62, #545559 and #616266 on the drawing and #4e4e4e, #464545 and #454546 on the datasheet's photograph. The drawing's reading is used because the drawing is the calibrated instrument for every other number on this face; the photograph is a lit product shot and reads about 15 counts darker throughout. It is darker than the AIS800-32D's measured #6a6b6e either way."},"the-port-lamps-are-one-round-window-each":{"confidence":"measured","note":"ONE LAMP PER PORT, ON THE POST TO THE LEFT OF ITS CAGE, and the first model of this device had a strip of eight along the bezel instead - a whole component was written for that and thrown away when the enlargement was read properly. THE ENLARGEMENT SETTLES IT. The guide's System LEDs/Buttons page draws the last four columns at 15.0 px/mm, three times the elevation's resolution. On every post it shows FOUR round dots about 1.0 mm across, at y 18.42, 37.20, 51.83 and 70.68 - one level with each of the four aperture rows. Scanned across the whole enlargement they appear at x 322.51, 346.50 and 370.49 against column left edges of 324.91, 348.93 and 372.95: 2.40 mm to the LEFT of each column, on the post it shares with the column before it. There is no dot 21.6 mm to the right of the last column, which is what decides that they belong to the cage on their right rather than the one on their left. THE LAMP PAIR IS SPREAD WIDER THAN THE PORT PAIR, and that is measured rather than tidied. Within a bank the lamps sit 18.78 and 18.85 mm apart where the apertures sit 17.51 apart, so each lamp is about half a millimetre outboard of its own port's centre - symmetric about the assembly, consistently on both banks, read at 15 px/mm. L61 says so sixty-four times and the baseline records it: the hardware is what it is, and moving the lamps onto the port centres would be drawing the rule rather than the panel. WHAT THE FOUR COLOURS MEAN IS THE PORT'S, NOT THE LAMP'S. The guide gives one legend for the port - \"QSFP-DD800 LEDs: Yellow (800G), Blue (400G), White (200G), Green (100G)\" - and there is exactly one window, so for once the colours and the windows agree: the lamp shows the port's negotiated rate. The four speed states are declared on the block's lamps and nothing is invented. This is the opposite of the AIS800-32D's case, where four windows shared one legend and the device had to waive L39 to say so."},"the-rear-closes-arithmetically":{"confidence":"measured","note":"AND IT WAS MEASURED TWICE, on the drawing at 5.06 px/mm and on the datasheet's rear photograph at 8.99, which is the check the 32-port models could not run. THE SUPPLIES ARE 73.5 x 40 AND THEY STACK. Vertical-edge scans put the housing's left edge at 15.0-15.3 on both sources and its right at 88.1-88.5; horizontal seams bound PSU1 at 4.54/43.84 on the drawing and 4.13/43.40 on the photograph, and PSU2 at 46.01/84.52 and 46.60/85.90. That is the CRPS 73.5 x 40 footprint, and the reads land on it within the drawing's half-pixel. THE TRAY PITCH IS 85.71 FROM THREE RAILS. The rails between trays read 176.16/180.50, 262.06/266.01 and 347.58/351.92 on the drawing and 176.0/180.24 and 261.43/265.67 on the photograph - a 4.2 mm rail on an 85.71 pitch (85.43 by the photograph), leaving 81.6 for the tray face. The block runs from 94.50 to 433.23 and the chassis frame picks up at 433.09. THE TRAYS ARE 81.2 TALL, from seams at 4.94 and 86.10 on the drawing and 4.13 and 85.88 on the photograph. THE BAYS ARE NUMBERED AND THIS TIME THE NUMERALS ARE LEGIBLE, which is what the AIS800-32D's fan-bay-numerals gap asked for and could not have. The photograph resolves a snowflake, a numeral and a right-pointing triangle silkscreened on each rail: 1, 2, 3 and 4 from LEFT to right, the opposite of edgecore/exp100-32x and edgecore/dcs240, which both number right to left. They are drawn."},"the-rj45s-are-not-all-the-same-way-up":{"confidence":"measured","note":"AND THE FIRST MODEL OF THIS DEVICE HAD ALL THREE THE SAME WAY UP. The guide's LED enlargement resolves each jack's keyway at 15 px/mm: MGMT has its latch slot at the TOP, CONSOLE has its latch slot at the TOP, and ToD - directly below CONSOLE in the same bezel - has it at the BOTTOM. The stacked pair is a mirrored module, which is the ordinary way a two-high RJ-45 assembly is built, and MGMT matches the upper of the two. std/rj45@2 draws tab-down, so MGMT and CONSOLE are placed `rotate: 180` and ToD is placed as drawn."},"the-rows-of-marks-above-each-cage-are-gasket-tabs-and-not-lamps":{"confidence":"measured","note":"FIVE EVENLY SPACED MARKS ALONG THE TOP EDGE OF EVERY CAGE ASSEMBLY, AND THE SAME ALONG THE BOTTOM, and they were asked about in review because at a glance they read as a row of small lamps. THEY ARE NOT LAMPS, ON FOUR COUNTS. The guide's System LEDs/Buttons page names every lamp on this face and there are exactly four kinds - \"QSFP-DD800 LEDs\", \"RJ-45 MGMT LEDs\", \"SFP28 LEDs\" and the six \"System LEDs\" - and the datasheet's own summary agrees (\"Port LEDs: Link Status, Activity, Rate\"). Five marks above and five below every port would be ten more per port and 640 on the face, legended nowhere. They appear on BOTH edges of each assembly, which no indicator does. They are grey metal with a chevron moulded into each, where every lamp on this face is a domed lens in a dark rim. And the enlargement resolves them at 15 px/mm as tabs standing on the cage's own flange, on a 3.66 mm pitch across the 18.28 mm cage. THEY ARE THE CAGE'S EMI GASKET FINGERS - the sprung tabs that ground a transceiver's shell to the cage as it slides in - which is why they ring the opening rather than sit beside it. BOTH ROWS ARE DRAWN, one at each end of every assembly, as a slot field on the cage shell. The first model drew only the top row, because the registry aperture hung from the drawn aperture's top edge left no room under the lower opening and L44 correctly called a bottom band buried; centring the aperture (above) gives both ends the same 0.8 mm and the rows come out symmetric. THE PORT LAMP IS THE SINGLE ROUND ONE ON THE POST, one per port, and it is a different thing in a different place. See the-port-lamps-are-one-round-window-each."},"the-triangles-are-printed-and-the-sfp-pair-s-are-not":{"confidence":"measured","note":"THE WALL'S ARROWS ARE SILKSCREEN. The sixty-four `(up)`/`(down)` glyphs beside the port numerals are solid white, the same white and the same crispness as the numerals they sit between, and every lamp on this face reads differently - a domed lens in a dark rim. This is the AIS800-32D's finding applied before the fact rather than after; see roc-ops/Portrayal#396, which is open on the EXP100 and EXP800 for the same marks. THE SFP28 PAIR'S TWO ARE LAMPS. The management cluster's SFP28 bezel carries a white band between its two cages with a `(up)` and a `(down)` moulded into it, and the guide's own callout 3 points at that band and names it: \"SFP28 LEDs: Green (link/activity)\". A glyph a vendor labels as a LED is a lamp, and common/led-arrow-sm@1 is the part. THE NUMERALS ARE 2.3 MM OF CAP HEIGHT, measured on the enlargement at 15 px/mm (rows 10.61-12.88), which is font-size 2.9 - not the 1.3 a first pass would guess."}},"references":[{"title":"Edgecore AIS800-64D 800 Gigabit AI & Data Center Ethernet Switch Quick Start Guide"},{"title":"Edgecore AIS800 Data Center Switch AIS800-64O/AIS800-64D Data Sheet"}],"version":"3.0.1","views":{"bottom":{"empty":"Not drawn by any staged source.
